### `symbols-docs` (1 pt)

Earned when at least 80% of exported symbols across the declared entrypoints
have a JSDoc comment. Computed via `deno doc --json`:
`documentedExports / totalExports ≥ 0.80`.

Counting rules:

- Only exported symbols count.
- Each symbol is counted once per declaration (function overloads count as
  separate declarations).
- A symbol is "documented" if its `jsDoc.doc` field is a non-empty string.
- Types, interfaces, classes, functions, and constants all count.

When `deno doc` cannot analyse the source, nothing counts as documented and the
remediation names that failure (`docAnalysisError`) instead of asking for JSDoc;
fix the failure first. `has-readme` likewise stops offering a module-level JSDoc
in place of a README until `deno doc` can analyse the source.

### `fast-check` (1 pt)

I fixed the failing check on PR #524 and pushed the fix, but CI hasn't run on it yet. Locally the extension now scores 100% on the quality gate, and check, lint, `fmt:check` and all 37 tests pass.

**Cause:** the `quality aws/securityhub-findings` job scored 92%, and the only factor it missed was `symbols-docs`. That factor needs JSDoc comments on at least 80% of the exported symbols. The PR exports three: `SortFieldSchema`, `SortOrderSchema` and `model`. `SortOrderSchema` was new in this PR and had no doc comment, so only 2 of 3 were documented (67%).

**Fix:** I added a JSDoc comment to `SortOrderSchema` in `aws/securityhub-findings/extensions/models/aws/securityhub_findings.ts`. The commit is `f6bba95e`, pushed to `fix/securityhub-sort-override` from the worktree at `.worktrees/fix-securityhub-sort-override`.

The PR already bumps the version to 2026.10.23.1 and has release notes, so this commit needed neither. All other checks had already passed.
